leads.title: Syariah Penal Code Order (SPCO)
leads.documents: Core legal status for LGBTQ: de jure death by stoning for liwat between married men if admit or 4 male adult Muslim eyewitnesses testify, otherwise 7 years + 30 strokes whipping; 1 year or 100 lashes for unmarried men; for sex between women combination of 40 lashes caning, up to 10 years prison, up to B$40,000 fine; bans men dressing as women / women as men 'without reasonable excuse' or 'for immoral purposes'
leads.detail: Cited as Syariah Penal Code Order / SPC / Sharia law with staged implementation from 2014, adultery and sodomy provisions scheduled 3 April 2019; no URL visible in excerpt

leads.title: Brunei Penal Code Order - Chapter 22, Secular Law on 'carnal intercourse against the order of nature'
leads.documents: Secular criminalization baseline before/parallel to SPCO: up to 10 years imprisonment for homosexual acts even if private consensual; July amendment increasing minimum to 20-50 years incarceration, primarily applied in male rape/child abuse cases
leads.detail: Cited as Chapter 22 of the Penal Code Order amended in July; no URL visible in excerpt

leads.title: 1906 Courts Enactment / Courts Enactment 1908 - Straits Settlements law application
leads.documents: Historical criminalization origin: same-sex activity became illegal in 1906 when Brunei became British Protectorate via Straits Settlements law, repealed/updated 1908; remained illegal after independence 1984
leads.detail: Cited as 1906 Courts Enactment and Courts Enactment 1908; no URL visible in excerpt

leads.title: U.S. Department of State - 2017 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Brunei
leads.documents: Enforcement and rights machinery: no known convictions that year; bans on liwat and cross-dressing; unofficial/societal discrimination in employment, housing, recreation, education; police intimidation/threats to out sexuality, block government jobs/graduation; government monitoring of activities/communications; permits denied for LGBTI events, restrictions on assembly/expression
leads.detail: Cited as '2017 United States Department of State report' section with full LGBTI excerpt; no URL visible in excerpt

leads.title: United Nations appeal to review Brunei Sharia laws
leads.documents: International human-rights machinery response when move to Sharia announced: UN urged Brunei to review laws described by media as 'medieval' and 'uncivilized'; implementation delayed until April 2019 after Sultan called laws 'special guidance' from God
leads.detail: Cited as United Nations urged Brunei to review its laws; no URL visible in excerpt

leads.title: OutRight Action International assessment of Brunei
leads.documents: Institutional human-rights assessment: described Brunei as 'the country that has the most worrisome state of rights for LGBT people in Southeast Asia'
leads.detail: Cited as OutRight Action International quote; no URL visible in excerpt

leads.title: The Brunei Project (est. 2015)
leads.documents: Local rights machinery/advocacy: promotes human rights including religious freedom, free speech, and LGBTQ rights via social media; organized private 2016 International Day Against Homophobia event - Brunei's first
leads.detail: Cited as The Brunei Project with External links entry 'The Brunei Project'; no URL visible in excerpt

leads.title: University of Brunei - 2011 formal study of gay people in Brunei
leads.documents: Living conditions/enforcement climate: illustrated choice to remain silent/discreet; researchers only found 29 LGBTQ respondents including foreigners, vs 460,345 total population in 2020; supports need for discretion
leads.detail: Cited as 2011 academics at University of Brunei study; no URL visible in excerpt

leads.title: 11 March 2015 Syariah cross-dressing enforcement case
leads.documents: Documented gender-expression enforcement directly relevant to trans visitors: civil servant fined B$1,000 under Syariah Penal Code Order for cross-dressing; plus policy that Brunei does not allow name/gender change on documents and does not allow sex reassignment surgery
leads.detail: Cited as 11 March 2015 B$1,000 fine under Syariah Penal Code Order; no URL visible in excerpt

leads.title: Brunei Government May 2019 moratorium extension to SPCO
leads.documents: Current de facto penalty status: after widespread condemnation including George Clooney open letter calling boycott of Sultan's hotels (Beverly Hills Hotel, Hotel Bel-Air), government extended death-penalty moratorium to SPCO; stoning not enacted while moratorium continues but could be lifted at any time by absolute monarch without warning; still in effect as of May 2023
leads.detail: Cited as May 2019 moratorium extension; Clooney letter and hotel names cited; no URL visible in excerpt
